newsitem.title: CHINA: China first quarter silk exports up 17.6 percent.
newsitem.headline: China first quarter silk exports up 17.6 percent.

text.p: China exported $538 million worth of silk products in the first quarter of this year, up 17.6 percent compared with the same period in 1996, the Securities Daily said on Thursday, quoting customs figures.
Silk industry output totalled 5.117 billion yuan ($616.5 million) in the first quarter, down a year-on-year 7.57 percent, the newspaper said.

Loss-making silk enterprises accounted for 59.4 percent of the industry in the first quarter, down 2.6 percentage points compared with the year-ago period, it said, quoting a survey of 20 major silk producing cities.
Silk industry losses totalled 200 million yuan in the first three months, it said.
China is trying to streamline its ailing silk industry and has vowed not to approve any new silk factories this year and to tighten renewal requirements for production licences.
China's silk industry has plunged since the second half of 1994 because of a chaotic supply of cocoons, overcapacity at silk-reeling plants and a price war among exporters.
In 1996, 80 percent of silk enterprises were losing money and frustrated cocoon-raisers had chopped down about 30 percent of their mulberry trees.
Cocoon output plunged 38 percent in 1996 to about 420,000 tonnes, earlier figures show.
China, the world's biggest producer and exporter of silk, exported $2.5 billion worth of silk products in 1996, down 18 percent from a year ago.
China is expected to export about 75 percent of all its silk products and 10,000 tonnes of raw silk this year.
